title: Calculations on reactions - 123 school
heading: Calculations on reactions
intro: All the data you need is in the question. Round to one decimal place if it does not say how.

questions.question: What does the law of conservation of mass state?

answers.a: A little mass always disappears in a reaction
answers.b: The mass of the reaction products is always greater than that of the reactants
answers.c: The total mass before the reaction is equal to the total mass after the reaction
answers.d: The mass of the reactants is always greater than that of the reaction products

questions.question: In a reaction in a closed bottle, 12 g of magnesium reacts with 8 g of oxygen. How many grams of magnesium oxide are formed?
When 10.0 g of limestone (CaCO<sub>3</sub>) is heated, 5.6 g of calcium oxide and carbon dioxide are formed. How many grams of carbon dioxide are formed?
You burn steel wool in the open air. The mass increases. Why is that?

answers.a: The steel wool takes up oxygen from the air
answers.b: New mass is created out of nothing
answers.d: The steel wool has acquired a lower density

questions.question: A candle burns in the open air and the mass decreases. Why is that?

answers.a: The candle is converted into energy and nothing else
answers.c: The gases formed, carbon dioxide and water vapour, escape into the air

questions.question: Calculate the molecular mass (or formula mass) of H<sub>2</sub>O. Atomic masses: H = 1.0 u, O = 16.0 u.
Calculate the molecular mass (or formula mass) of CO<sub>2</sub>. Atomic masses: C = 12.0 u, O = 16.0 u.
Calculate the molecular mass (or formula mass) of NH<sub>3</sub>. Atomic masses: N = 14.0 u, H = 1.0 u.
Calculate the molecular mass (or formula mass) of H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub>. Atomic masses: H = 1.0 u, S = 32.0 u, O = 16.0 u.
Calculate the molecular mass (or formula mass) of CaCO<sub>3</sub>. Atomic masses: Ca = 40.0 u, C = 12.0 u, O = 16.0 u.
Calculate the molecular mass (or formula mass) of Ca(OH)<sub>2</sub>. Atomic masses: Ca = 40.0 u, O = 16.0 u, H = 1.0 u.
Calculate the molecular mass (or formula mass) of Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>. Atomic masses: Fe = 56.0 u, O = 16.0 u.
Calculate the mass percentage of carbon in CO<sub>2</sub>. Atomic masses: C = 12.0 u, O = 16.0 u.
Calculate the mass percentage of oxygen in H<sub>2</sub>O. Atomic masses: H = 1.0 u, O = 16.0 u.
Calculate the mass percentage of iron in Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>. Atomic masses: Fe = 56.0 u, O = 16.0 u.
Hydrogen and oxygen react to form water: 2 H<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> → 2 H<sub>2</sub>O. Atomic masses: H = 1.0 u, O = 16.0 u. How many grams of water are formed from 4.0 g of hydrogen?
Carbon burns to form carbon dioxide: C + O<sub>2</sub> → CO<sub>2</sub>. Atomic masses: C = 12.0 u, O = 16.0 u. How many grams of carbon dioxide are formed from 12.0 g of carbon?
Limestone is heated: CaCO<sub>3</sub> → CaO + CO<sub>2</sub>. Atomic masses: Ca = 40.0 u, C = 12.0 u, O = 16.0 u. How many grams of calcium oxide are formed from 50.0 g of limestone?
Magnesium burns: 2 Mg + O<sub>2</sub> → 2 MgO. Atomic masses: Mg = 24.0 u, O = 16.0 u. How many grams of magnesium oxide are formed from 12.0 g of magnesium?
Magnesium and oxygen react in the mass ratio 3 : 2. How many grams of oxygen are needed for 9.0 g of magnesium?
Copper and sulfur react to form copper(I) sulfide in the mass ratio 4 : 1. How many grams of copper(I) sulfide are formed from 8.0 g of copper and 2.0 g of sulfur?
Iron and sulfur react in the mass ratio 7 : 4. How many grams of sulfur do you need for 14 g of iron?
The molar mass of water is 18 g/mol. How many moles of water are in 36 g of water?
The molar mass of CO<sub>2</sub> is 44 g/mol. How many moles of CO<sub>2</sub> are in 4.4 g of CO<sub>2</sub>?
The molar mass of NaCl is 58.5 g/mol. How many grams of NaCl is 0.40 mol?
The molar mass of H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> is 98 g/mol. How many moles is 49 g of H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub>?
In the reaction 2 H<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> → 2 H<sub>2</sub>O, 3.0 mol of H<sub>2</sub> reacts. How many moles of H<sub>2</sub>O are formed?
In the reaction 2 H<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> → 2 H<sub>2</sub>O, 4.0 mol of H<sub>2</sub> reacts. How many moles of O<sub>2</sub> are needed for this?
In the reaction N<sub>2</sub> + 3 H<sub>2</sub> → 2 NH<sub>3</sub>, 6.0 mol of H<sub>2</sub> reacts. How many moles of NH<sub>3</sub> are formed?
In the reaction 2 Mg + O<sub>2</sub> → 2 MgO, 0.50 mol of Mg reacts. How many moles of MgO are formed?
What does a molar mass of 18 g/mol mean for water?

answers.a: One mole of water has a mass of 18 g
answers.b: One molecule of water has a mass of 18 g
answers.c: Water has a density of 18 g/cm<sup>3</sup>
answers.d: 18 mol of water has a mass of 1 g

questions.question: What is the mass of 2.0 mol of CO<sub>2</sub>? Molar mass of CO<sub>2</sub> = 44 g/mol.
What can you read from 2 H<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> → 2 H<sub>2</sub>O?

answers.a: 2 mol H<sub>2</sub> reacts with 2 mol O<sub>2</sub> to give 2 mol H<sub>2</sub>O
answers.b: 2 mol H<sub>2</sub> and 1 mol O<sub>2</sub> give 3 mol H<sub>2</sub>O
answers.c: 1 mol H<sub>2</sub> reacts with 1 mol O<sub>2</sub> to give 1 mol H<sub>2</sub>O
answers.d: 2 mol of H<sub>2</sub> reacts with 1 mol of O<sub>2</sub> to form 2 mol of H<sub>2</sub>O
